title: Kidney Emergencies and the Dialysis Patient

slides.title: Today's lesson
slides.body:
As an EMR you already assess abdominal pain, give oxygen, position for comfort and transport. Today, as a PCP:

  1. Understand AKI and CKD, and why failing kidneys raise potassium
  2. Care for dialysis patients: the access arm, fluids, emergencies
  3. Handle stones, UTIs and GU trauma with your new PCP tools

Textbook: Chapter 35, PDF pages 3045–3093
slides.say: Welcome to class. Today's topic is the kidneys and the urinary system. As EMRs, you already assess abdominal and flank pain, give oxygen, position patients for comfort, and transport. As a PCP, these patients get more complicated, because now you start IVs, give fluids and give more drugs, and kidney patients react differently to all three. Today we'll cover three things: acute and chronic kidney disease, and why failing kidneys let potassium build up; how to care for dialysis patients safely; and how to handle kidney stones, urinary infections and genitourinary trauma with your new PCP tools.
slides.sayZh: 欢迎来上课。今天讲肾脏和泌尿系统。作为 EMR，你们已经会评估腹痛和腰痛、给氧、摆舒适体位、转运。作为 PCP，这些病人变得更复杂，因为你现在要开静脉、补液、给更多的药，而肾病病人对这三样的反应都和别人不同。今天讲三件事：急性和慢性肾病，以及为什么肾衰竭会让钾蓄积；怎样安全地照护透析病人；以及怎样用 PCP 的新工具处理肾结石、尿路感染和泌尿生殖系统创伤。

slides.title: What the kidneys do
slides.body:
• Filter about 200 L of blood a day; GFR about 125 mL/min
  • Receive about one quarter of the cardiac output
  • Balance water, electrolytes and pH; clear wastes and drugs
  • BP falls → renin → angiotensin II → vessels squeeze, salt kept
  • Aldosterone keeps sodium and gets rid of potassium
slides.say: Let's start with what the kidneys do. They filter about two hundred litres of blood a day, at a filtration rate, or GFR, of about one hundred twenty-five millilitres a minute, and they receive about a quarter of the heart's output. They balance water, electrolytes and acid, and clear wastes and drugs. They also defend the blood pressure: when it falls, the kidney releases renin, which leads to angiotensin two; that squeezes the vessels and holds on to salt and water. The hormone aldosterone keeps sodium and gets rid of potassium. Remember that last point: when the kidneys fail, potassium builds up, and it can stop the heart.
slides.sayZh: 先看肾脏做什么。肾每天过滤约两百升血液，滤过率也就是 GFR 约每分钟一百二十五毫升，接收的血流约占心输出量的四分之一。肾平衡水、电解质和酸碱，清除废物和药物。它还守护血压：血压下降时，肾释放肾素，最终生成血管紧张素二，让血管收紧、保留盐和水。醛固酮这种激素保钠、排钾。记住最后这点：肾衰竭时钾会蓄积，而高钾可以让心脏停跳。

slides.title: Acute kidney injury: three places
slides.body:
Prerenalnot enough blood inbleeding, dehydration, shock, sepsis, heart failure
Intrarenalthe kidney itselflow-flow damage, toxins, drugs, rhabdomyolysis
Postrenalurine can't get outbig prostate, stones, clots

AKI develops over days and is often reversible. Oliguria: under 500 mL of urine a day.
slides.say: Acute kidney injury, or AKI, used to be called acute renal failure. Filtration drops suddenly, over days, and toxins build up. Think of it by location. Prerenal means not enough blood reaches the kidney: bleeding, dehydration, shock, sepsis, or heart failure. This is where you have the most effect, because restoring perfusion in time often reverses it. Intrarenal means damage to the kidney itself, from long periods of low flow, toxins, some drugs, or muscle breakdown, called rhabdomyolysis. Postrenal means urine can't get out, because of an enlarged prostate, stones, or clots. Less than five hundred millilitres of urine a day is called oliguria. Untreated, AKI leads to fluid overload, high potassium, and acidosis.
slides.sayZh: 急性肾损伤，即 AKI，以前叫急性肾衰竭：滤过在几天内骤降，毒素在体内蓄积。按部位来记。肾前性是流到肾的血不够：出血、脱水、休克、脓毒症或心衰。这是你最能影响的一类，因为及时恢复灌注常常可以逆转。肾性是肾脏本身受损，原因有长时间低灌注、毒素、某些药物，或肌肉溶解，也就是横纹肌溶解。肾后性是尿排不出去，原因有前列腺增大、结石或血块。每天尿量少于五百毫升叫少尿。AKI 不治疗会导致液体过多、高钾和酸中毒。

slides.title: Chronic kidney disease
slides.body:
• Months to years; nephrons destroyed; not reversible
  • More than half: diabetes or high blood pressure
  • Signs: edema, itching, pale skin, weakness, uremic frost
  • Ask: "Do you still make urine?"
  • Drugs act longer and stronger: avoid non-essential meds
slides.say: Chronic kidney disease, or CKD, develops over months or years. The nephrons, the kidney's filtering units, are permanently destroyed, so it doesn't reverse. More than half of all cases come from diabetes or high blood pressure, so those two words in a history should make you think about the kidneys. Waste builds up in the blood, which is called uremia. You may see swelling of the face and limbs, itching, pale skin, weakness, and sometimes a white crust on the face called uremic frost. Ask whether the patient still makes urine. And as a PCP who now gives more drugs, remember: kidney patients clear drugs slowly, so effects last longer and hit harder.
slides.sayZh: 慢性肾脏病，即 CKD，在几个月到几年里形成。肾单位，也就是肾的过滤单位，被永久毁损，所以不能逆转。一半以上的病例由糖尿病或高血压引起，所以病史里看到这两个词就要想到肾。废物在血中蓄积叫尿毒症。你可能看到面部和四肢水肿、皮肤瘙痒、苍白、乏力，有时脸上还有一层白色结晶，叫尿素霜。要问病人还有没有尿。作为现在要给更多药的 PCP，要记住：肾病病人清除药物慢，药效更久也更强。

slides.title: Dialysis: two kinds
slides.body:
PeritonealHemodialysis
Howfluid in the belly, drained after 4–6 hblood through a machine
Whencan be done at homeevery 2–3 days, for 3–5 h
Main riskperitonitis: keep it sterilethe access; fluid and K⁺ shifts

Home dialysis? The patient and family often know the machine best. Ask them.
slides.say: Dialysis does the kidneys' job when they can't: it removes waste and extra fluid and resets the electrolytes. There are two kinds. In peritoneal dialysis, special fluid runs into the abdomen, stays for four to six hours while waste moves into it, then drains out. It can be done at home, and the big risk is peritonitis, a dangerous infection, so keep everything clean. In hemodialysis, blood flows out through a surgically made access, through a machine, and back in. It usually happens every two or three days, for three to five hours. Home dialysis patients and their families often know the machine better than you, so ask them.
slides.sayZh: 透析在肾脏不能工作时替它干活：清除废物和多余液体，并恢复电解质平衡。透析分两种。腹膜透析是把专用透析液灌进腹腔，留置四到六小时，让废物进入液体，然后放出。它可以在家做，最大风险是腹膜炎这种危险的感染，所以一切都要保持无菌。血液透析是血液通过手术建立的通路流出，经过机器再流回体内，通常每两三天一次，每次三到五小时。在家透析的病人和家属往往比你更懂机器，所以要问他们。

slides.title: The access arm: hands off
slides.body:
Fistula or shunt arm: no BP cuff, no IV

  • AV fistula: artery joined to a vein, forearm or upper arm
  • Often a visible bulge under the skin; ask the patient
  • A cuff for a few minutes can clot it
  • An IV can infect it, damage it, and use up future veins
  • Take the BP and start the IV on the other arm
slides.say: This is the rule you must never break. A hemodialysis patient's lifeline is the access, often an AV fistula, a direct connection between an artery and a vein in the forearm or upper arm. You'll usually see a bulge under the skin, and the patient will tell you about it. Never put a blood pressure cuff on that arm: blocking the flow for even a few minutes can make it clot. And now that you start IVs, never put an IV in that arm either. It can bring infection, damage the access, and use up veins the patient may need for future access. Take the blood pressure and start your IV on the other arm, every time.
slides.sayZh: 这是一条绝对不能破的规矩。血透病人的生命线是透析通路，常见的是动静脉内瘘，也就是在前臂或上臂把动脉和静脉直接接起来。你通常能看到皮下鼓起一条，病人也会告诉你。绝不能在那只手臂上绑血压袖带：阻断血流哪怕几分钟，都可能让它形成血栓。现在你要开静脉了，也绝不能在那只手臂上开：可能带进感染、损坏通路，还会用掉病人将来做通路需要的血管。测血压、开静脉，每次都用另一只手臂。

slides.q: A hemodialysis patient with a left forearm fistula is pale and hypotensive after dialysis. You're the PCP. Where do you take the BP and start the IV?
options: Left arm for both: the fistula vein is big and easy
Left arm for the IV, right arm for the BP
Skip the BP and use the fistula itself for the IV
slides.say: Let's pause for a question. A hemodialysis patient with a fistula in the left forearm is pale and hypotensive after dialysis. You're the PCP. Where do you take the blood pressure and start the IV? A, the left arm for both, because the fistula vein is big and easy. B, the left arm for the IV, and the right arm for the blood pressure. C, the right arm for both. D, skip the blood pressure and use the fistula itself for the IV. Tap your answer.
slides.sayZh: 停一下考考你：一位左前臂有内瘘的血透病人，透析后脸色苍白、血压低。你是 PCP，在哪里测血压、开静脉？A 都用左臂，因为内瘘的血管又粗又好扎；B 左臂开静脉，右臂测血压；C 都用右臂；D 不测血压，直接用内瘘开静脉。点选你的答案。
slides.explain: The answer is C, the right arm for both. The fistula arm gets no blood pressure cuff and no IV. A cuff can make the fistula clot, and an IV can infect or damage it and use up veins the patient needs for future access. A and B both put something on the fistula arm. D is wrong too: the fistula is not your IV site, and you still need a blood pressure, especially in a hypotensive patient.
slides.explainZh: 答案是 C，两样都用右臂。内瘘那只手臂不绑袖带、不开静脉。袖带可能让内瘘形成血栓，静脉穿刺可能带来感染或损坏通路，还会用掉病人将来需要的血管。A 和 B 都在内瘘侧手臂上操作。D 也错：内瘘不是你开静脉的地方，而且你仍然需要血压，低血压病人更是如此。

slides.title: Dialysis emergencies
slides.body:
• Low BP during or just after dialysis: dizzy, confused, yawning
  • Bleeding at the access: direct pressure; clamp if it's come apart
  • Disequilibrium: headache, vomiting, confusion → transport
  • Can't tell it from a subdural bleed on scene
  • Air embolism: sudden SOB, low BP, cyanosis
  • → clamp, disconnect, left side, head down about 10°
slides.say: Dialysis itself can cause emergencies. Low blood pressure during or right after a session is common and can lead to arrest; watch for dizziness, confusion, and a lot of yawning. Bleeding at the access needs direct pressure; if the line has come apart, clamp it. In disequilibrium syndrome, water shifts into the brain after dialysis: headache, vomiting and confusion. You can't tell it from a subdural bleed on scene, so transport. If a fitting comes loose, air can enter: sudden shortness of breath, low pressure, cyanosis. Clamp, disconnect, and lay the patient on the left side, head down about ten degrees, to keep the air in the right heart.
slides.sayZh: 透析本身也会引发急症。透析中或刚结束时低血压很常见，可能导致心搏骤停；注意头晕、意识混乱和频繁打哈欠。通路出血用直接压迫；管路脱开就夹闭。失衡综合征是透析后水移进大脑，表现为头痛、呕吐、意识混乱。现场无法和硬膜下出血区分，所以要转运。接头松了空气可能进入：突然气短、血压低、发绀。要夹闭、断开机器，让病人左侧卧、头低约十度，把空气留在右心。

slides.title: High potassium: watch the ECG
slides.body:
Missed dialysis + weakness → think high K⁺

peaked T→P flattens, disappears→wide QRS→sine wave→arrest

No BC exam drug is indicated for it: recognize, notify early, move fast, be ready for arrest.
slides.say: The most dangerous problem in kidney failure is high potassium, or hyperkalemia. The kidneys can't get rid of it, so it climbs, especially after missed dialysis, and the patient often feels profoundly weak. The ECG changes in a set order: tall, peaked T waves; then the P wave flattens and disappears; then the QRS widens until the tracing looks like a sine wave; then a dead rhythm or asystole. That's why the book wants every renal patient on a cardiac monitor. The hospital drugs for it aren't on the BC exam drug list, so your job is early recognition, an early call, fast transport, and readiness for arrest.
slides.sayZh: 肾衰竭最危险的问题是高血钾。肾排不出钾，钾就不断升高，尤其是漏了透析之后，病人常常极度乏力。心电图按固定顺序变化：先是高尖的 T 波；接着 P 波变平、消失；然后 QRS 增宽，直到波形像正弦波；接下来就是无效心律或心脏停搏。所以书里要求每个肾病病人都上心电监护。医院治疗高钾的药不在 BC 考试药物清单上，所以你的任务是早识别、早通知、快转运，并做好复苏准备。

slides.title: Kidney stones and UTIs
slides.body:
• Stone: vague flank ache, severe within 30–60 min
  • Pain moves from the flank toward the groin
  • Restless "kidney stone dance" vs. lying still (peritonitis)
  • UTI: burning, frequency, urgency; fever + flank pain = kidney
  • Older adult with new confusion: think UTI
  • Fluids help suspected sepsis, but don't flush out a stone
slides.say: Two common calls. A kidney stone usually starts as a vague ache in the flank and becomes severe within thirty to sixty minutes. As the stone moves down, the pain moves forward toward the groin. These patients can't get comfortable and keep shifting, the so-called kidney stone dance; a patient with peritonitis lies very still instead. A urinary tract infection, or UTI, causes burning, frequency, and urgency; add fever, chills and flank pain, and the kidney is involved. In older adults, a UTI may show up only as weakness and confusion. For suspected sepsis, fluids help. For a stone, a fluid bolus doesn't push it out and may increase the pain.
slides.sayZh: 两类常见出诊。肾结石通常从腰部隐约不适开始，三十到六十分钟内变得剧烈；结石往下走，疼痛就往前移向腹股沟。这类病人找不到舒服的姿势，动个不停，就是所谓的「结石舞」；腹膜炎病人则一动不动。尿路感染，即 UTI，表现为排尿灼痛、尿频、尿急；再加上发热、寒战和腰痛，就是累及肾脏了。老年人的 UTI 可能只表现为乏力和意识混乱。疑似脓毒症时补液有帮助；但对结石，快速补液不能把它冲出来，还可能加重疼痛。

slides.q: You're a PCP. A healthy 40-year-old has left flank pain moving to the groin, pain 9/10, vomiting, BP 150/90. Which plan is best?
options: A 1 L fluid bolus to flush out the stone
No pain relief, so the hospital can assess him
Comfort position, consider an IV and an antiemetic, analgesia in scope
slides.say: Now a PCP decision. You're a PCP. A healthy forty-year-old has left flank pain moving to the groin. His pain is nine out of ten, he's vomiting, and his blood pressure is one fifty over ninety. Which plan is best? A, a one-litre fluid bolus to flush out the stone. B, no pain relief, so the hospital can assess him. C, a position of comfort, consider an IV and an antiemetic, and give analgesia within your scope. D, ASA, one hundred sixty milligrams, for the pain. Tap your answer.
slides.sayZh: 来一道 PCP 决策题。你是 PCP，一位平素健康的四十岁男士左侧腰痛并向腹股沟移动，疼痛九分，呕吐，血压一百五十比九十。哪个方案最好？A 快速输一升液体把结石冲出来；B 不给镇痛，方便医院评估；C 舒适体位，考虑开静脉和止吐药，并在执业范围内给镇痛；D 给 ASA 一百六十毫克止痛。点选你的答案。
slides.explain: The answer is C. Pain relief is the core of stone care; the book calls withholding it to protect the diagnosis a myth, so B is wrong. As a PCP, the BC nausea and vomiting protocol lets you consider an IV and an antiemetic. A is wrong because a bolus doesn't help a stone pass and may add pain. D is wrong because in BC, ASA is only for suspected cardiac chest pain or ischemia.
slides.explainZh: 答案是 C。镇痛是结石处理的核心；书里说为了不影响诊断而不给镇痛是一种误区，所以 B 错。作为 PCP，BC 恶心呕吐流程让你可以考虑开静脉和止吐药。A 错，快速补液不能帮助排石，反而可能加重疼痛。D 错，在 BC，ASA 只用于疑似心源性胸痛或心肌缺血。

slides.title: GU trauma: think beyond the obvious
slides.body:
• Lower ribs, flank, abdomen, pelvis or thighs hit → think GU
  • Kidney: flank bruise, low rib fractures; blood in urine found later
  • Bladder: pelvic fracture, lap-belt bruise, can't void, urethral blood
  • Big flank bruise or low BP, no outside bleeding → internal bleeding
  • Genitals: gentle pressure, ice; don't remove a trapped ring
slides.say: Genitourinary, or GU, trauma is easy to miss. Think of it whenever the lower ribs, flank, abdomen, pelvis or upper thighs are hit. Kidney injuries take big forces, like a fall from height or a high-speed crash. Look for flank bruising and lower rib fractures; blood in the urine usually isn't found until hospital. Suspect the bladder with a pelvic fracture or a lap-belt bruise, especially if the patient can't pass urine or has blood at the urethral opening. A big flank bruise or low blood pressure with no outside bleeding means internal bleeding. For genital injuries, use gentle pressure and ice, and never try to remove a trapped ring.
slides.sayZh: 泌尿生殖系统，即 GU 的创伤很容易漏掉。只要下位肋骨、腰部、腹部、骨盆或大腿上部受伤，就要想到它。肾损伤需要很大的力量，比如高处坠落或高速车祸。看腰部有没有瘀斑、下位肋骨有没有骨折；血尿通常到医院才查出来。骨盆骨折或下腹有安全带瘀斑时要怀疑膀胱伤，尤其是病人尿不出来或尿道口有血时。腰部大片瘀斑或血压低却没有外出血，就意味着内出血。生殖器损伤用轻柔压迫和冰敷，绝不要试图取下卡住的环。

slides.title: EMR vs PCP: the renal patient in BC
slides.body:
BC has no kidney protocol. Use what fits: Hypovolemia, Abdominal Injuries, Nausea–Vomiting, CHF.

All licence levels (EMR + PCP)

  • Primary survey; O₂ to SpO₂ ≥ 94%
  • Position of comfort; ready for vomiting
  • Bleeding: control it, lie supine, keep warm
  • Fluid overload (CHF): sit upright, legs down
  • Pain relief with EMR-level drugs if no contraindication

PCP adds

  • Vascular access; correct hypoperfusion
  • Bolus 20 mL/kg, max 2 L, reassess every 500 mL
  • TXA if indicated for traumatic bleeding
  • Nausea: consider ondansetron or dimenhydrinate
  • CHF: consider CPAP
  • Functional enquiry, incl. GI/GU (PCP only)
slides.say: BC has no kidney protocol, so combine the ones that fit. On the left, every licence level: a primary survey, oxygen to ninety-four percent, a comfortable position with suction ready, and for bleeding, control it, lay the patient flat and keep them warm. A dialysis patient in fluid overload falls under the heart failure protocol: sit upright, legs down. The PCP adds vascular access and, for shock, twenty millilitres per kilogram up to two litres, reassessing every five hundred, plus TXA for traumatic bleeding when indicated. You can also consider ondansetron or dimenhydrinate for nausea, CPAP for heart failure, and a functional enquiry that includes the GU system.
slides.sayZh: BC 没有专门的肾脏流程，所以要组合适用的流程。左栏是所有级别都做的：初步评估、给氧到九十四以上、舒适体位并备好吸引；有出血就控制出血、平卧、保暖。透析病人液体过多时按心衰流程处理：坐直、双腿下垂。PCP 多出的是：建立静脉通路；休克时按每公斤二十毫升、最多两升补液，每五百毫升复评一次；创伤出血符合指征时给 TXA。你还可以对恶心考虑昂丹司琼或茶苯海明，对心衰考虑 CPAP，系统问诊也要包括泌尿生殖系统。

slides.title: New for you as a PCP: watch out for
slides.body:
• No BP cuff and no IV on the fistula or shunt arm
  • Dialysis/CKD shock: fluid with caution; check lungs every 500 mL
  • Methoxyflurane: not with significant kidney impairment
  • Ibuprofen: consider another option with a kidney history
  • Entonox: not with a suspected air embolism
  • Nothing by mouth; drugs last longer in kidney failure
slides.say: Here are the new risks that come with your new tools. First, the access arm: no cuff and no IV, ever. Second, fluids. A dialysis or CKD patient can't get rid of extra water, so a bolus can flood the lungs. If they're in shock, give fluid cautiously, and at every five hundred millilitres, listen for crackles and look for swelling. Third, pain drugs. In BC, methoxyflurane is contraindicated with significant kidney impairment, and ibuprofen calls for another option in patients with a kidney history. Fourth, Entonox is contraindicated with an air embolism, which is a dialysis risk. And give nothing by mouth, and remember that drugs last longer when the kidneys fail.
slides.sayZh: 下面是新工具带来的新风险。第一，透析通路那只手臂：永远不绑袖带、不开静脉。第二，补液。透析或 CKD 病人排不掉多余的水，快速补液可能让肺里灌满水。休克时要谨慎补液，每五百毫升都听有没有湿啰音、看有没有水肿。第三，镇痛药。在 BC，明显肾功能损害时禁用甲氧氟烷，有肾病史的病人用布洛芬要考虑换别的方案。第四，空气栓塞时禁用笑气，而空气栓塞正是透析的风险之一。另外，禁止经口进食，并记住肾衰竭时药效更久。

slides.title: For the BC exam
slides.body:
• Book: opioids, ketorolac for stone pain → not on the BC exam (BCEHS added scope)
  • Book: calcium, bicarbonate for high K⁺ → not on the exam list
  • Salbutamol in BC: for bronchospasm, not for potassium
  • Book: atropine for slow rhythms → not on the BC exam
  • Book: OPQRST for pain → BC: OPQRRRST or LOTARP
  • EMRs: no IV. Lungs: at least 6 sites front or 6 back
slides.say: Let's compare the book with BC. For stone pain, the book uses opioids and ketorolac; neither is on the BC licensing exam, though BCEHS PCPs may give them after added-scope training. For high potassium, the book mentions calcium, salbutamol and bicarbonate. Calcium and bicarbonate aren't on the BC exam drug list, and in BC, salbutamol is for bronchospasm, not potassium. The book treats slow rhythms from low potassium with atropine, which isn't on the BC exam either. For the pain history, BC scoring expects OPQRRRST or LOTARP rather than the book's OPQRST. EMRs have no IV access. And when you listen for fluid in the lungs, BC wants at least six sites on the front or six on the back.
slides.sayZh: 把书和 BC 比一比。结石疼痛书里用阿片类和酮咯酸，两者执照考试都不考；BCEHS 的 PCP 经扩展范围（Schedule 1/2）培训后可以用。高钾时书里提到钙剂、沙丁胺醇和碳酸氢钠；钙剂和碳酸氢钠不在 BC 考试药物清单上，而在 BC，沙丁胺醇是用于支气管痉挛的，不是用于降钾。书里用阿托品治疗低钾引起的慢心律，这执照考试也不考。问疼痛病史，BC 评分要求用 OPQRRRST 或 LOTARP，而不是书里的 OPQRST。EMR 没有静脉权限。听诊肺部有没有积液时，BC 要求至少前胸六个点或后背六个点。

slides.title: Three things to remember
slides.body:
1. Fistula or shunt arm: no BP cuff, no IV
  2. Missed dialysis + weakness + peaked T = high K⁺: notify, move
  3. Stones: treat the pain, not with fluid; dialysis: fluid with caution

Next: Chapter 36, Toxicology: Substance Abuse and Poisoning
slides.say: Let's wrap up with three things to remember. One: on a dialysis patient, the fistula or shunt arm gets no blood pressure cuff and no IV, ever. Two: missed dialysis, profound weakness and peaked T waves mean high potassium until proven otherwise; notify early and transport fast. Three: for a kidney stone, treat the pain and the nausea, and don't use fluid to flush the stone; for a dialysis or CKD patient in shock, give fluid with caution and check the lungs every five hundred millilitres. Next chapter: toxicology, substance abuse and poisoning. If anything was unclear, tap Ask. See you next class.
slides.sayZh: 收尾三句话。一，透析病人内瘘或分流那只手臂，永远不绑血压袖带、不开静脉。二，漏了透析、极度乏力、T 波高尖，在排除之前都按高钾处理：早通知、快转运。三，肾结石要处理疼痛和恶心，不要靠补液冲石；透析或 CKD 病人休克时要谨慎补液，每五百毫升检查一次肺部。下一章讲毒理学：物质滥用与中毒。有不懂的点「Ask」。下节课见。
